title: What price and how many dosas give a profit of 2000 rupees?
description: A dosa cart pays rent of five thousand rupees a day, and each dosa costs ten rupees to make. A letter for the price gives eighty rupees for one hundred dosas, and a letter for the number sold gives one hundred seventy five dosas at fifty rupees.
teaching_notes: One idea: profit is income take away all the costs, so a letter makes an equation in both parts. Watch for students who forget the making cost in part one, or the rent in part two.

video_script.why: The child uses the profit equation from the lemonade stall twice: once with a letter for the price, and once with a letter for the number sold.
video_script.substitution: (i) Let p be the price: 100p − (5000 + 100 × 10) = 2000, so p = 80. (ii) Let n be the number sold: (50 − 10) n − 5000 = 2000, so n = 175.
video_script.anchor: a dosa cart with rent 5000 rupees a day and 10 rupees to make each dosa, profit 2000 rupees wanted
video_script.payoff_line: The answers are eighty rupees for each dosa, and one hundred seventy five dosas a day

final_answer.value: (i) ₹80 for each dosa (ii) 175 dosas a day
final_answer.spoken: the answers are eighty rupees for each dosa, and one hundred seventy five dosas a day

maths_rules: (i) let p be the price; income 100p; costs 5000 + 100 × 10 = 6000
(ii) each dosa earns 50 − 10 = 40 after its own cost; let n be the number sold
video_script.design: One idea: profit is income take away all the costs, used once for the price and once for the number sold. The costs stay on the board and each part ends with a check.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. A person runs a small dosa cart.
<bookmark mark='costs'/>The rent is five thousand rupees each day. Making one dosa costs ten rupees.
<bookmark mark='one'/>In part one, one hundred dosas are sold in a day. What price gives a profit of two thousand rupees?
<bookmark mark='two'/>In part two, customers pay only fifty rupees for a dosa. How many dosas must be sold for the same profit?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: income = price × number sold; profit = income − costs

marks.income: income = price × number sold is written

narration: <bookmark mark='income'/>The income is the price times the number of dosas sold.
<bookmark mark='profit'/>The profit is the income take away all the costs.

beats.on_screen: Given: rent ₹5000 a day; ₹10 to make each dosa; profit wanted ₹2000

marks.given: the three given numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, rent of five thousand rupees each day, and ten rupees to make each dosa. The profit wanted is two thousand rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: (i) the price of a dosa; (ii) the number of dosas sold

marks.find: the two aims are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the price for part one, and the number of dosas for part two.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, part (i): let p = the price; income = 100p; costs = 5000 + 100 × 10 = 6000

marks.let: p is written as the price of a dosa and income 100p is written

beats.colours: rent and making cost in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='let'/>Step one, part one. Let pee rupees be the price of one dosa, so one hundred dosas bring in one hundred pee.
<bookmark mark='costs'/>The costs are the rent of five thousand, and one hundred times ten, which is one thousand. In all, that is six thousand rupees.

marks.add: 6000 is added to both sides to give 100p = 8000

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step two, the profit is the income take away the costs. That gives one hundred pee take away six thousand, equal to two thousand.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add six thousand to both sides, and one hundred pee is eight thousand.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Divide eight thousand by one hundred, and pee is eighty.
<bookmark mark='income'/>Step three, check part one. One hundred dosas at eighty rupees bring in eight thousand rupees.
<bookmark mark='profit'/>Eight thousand take away six thousand is two thousand, the profit we wanted.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, part (ii): each dosa earns 50 − 10 = 40; let n = the dosas sold; 40n − 5000 = 2000

marks.earn: 50 − 10 = 40 is written as the earning of each dosa
marks.let: n is written as the number of dosas sold

narration: <bookmark mark='earn'/>Step four, part two. Each dosa sells for fifty rupees and costs ten to make, so it earns forty rupees.
<bookmark mark='let'/>Let en be the number of dosas sold, so they earn forty en.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>The profit is forty en take away the rent of five thousand, and this is two thousand.

marks.add: 5000 is added to both sides to give 40n = 7000

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step five, add five thousand to both sides, and forty en is seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Divide seven thousand by forty, and en is one hundred seventy five.
<bookmark mark='earn'/>Step six, check part two. One hundred seventy five dosas earning forty rupees each make seven thousand rupees.
<bookmark mark='profit'/>Seven thousand take away the rent of five thousand is two thousand.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (i) ₹80 for each dosa (ii) 175 dosas a day

marks.ans: the answers to both parts are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The answers are eighty rupees for each dosa, and one hundred seventy five dosas a day.
